# Filosofía KDD

Estas son las propiedades que conserva esta implementación. Los mecanismos
concretos se diseñan con Entire y deben demostrar que producen esas propiedades.

## Intención explícita

El trabajo responde a un problema y un resultado esperado comprensibles. Los
criterios de aceptación se acuerdan antes de delegar la implementación. Una
decisión de producto pertenece a quien tiene autoridad para tomarla.

## Conocimiento conectado al trabajo

Requisitos, decisiones, razones y evidencias deben poder encontrarse desde el
trabajo al que pertenecen. El contexto se transmite con procedencia y límites,
y se contrasta con el estado actual antes de reutilizarlo.

## Verificación independiente

Quien implementa no concede por sí solo la aprobación de su resultado. Los
criterios, pruebas y controles acordados no se cambian para fabricar un resultado
favorable. Un cambio legítimo de esos criterios requiere revisión independiente.

## Alcance comprobable

La delegación define qué se puede modificar y qué requiere una nueva decisión.
La revisión considera los cambios reales. Escribir una restricción en un prompt
no demuestra que se haya aplicado.

## Evidencia antes que declaraciones

Una tarea no se considera verificada porque un agente diga que terminó. La
evidencia debe identificar qué se ejecutó, sobre qué revisión, con qué resultado
y con qué limitaciones. La ausencia de evidencia no equivale a una aprobación.

## Juicio y comprobación con funciones distintas

La revisión humana y la evaluación de agentes ayudan a detectar problemas y
valorar el producto. Las propiedades susceptibles de comprobación determinista
requieren comprobaciones efectivamente ejecutadas. La combinación debe mantener
visible qué demuestra cada resultado.

## Cierre trazable

La entrega conserva su vínculo con la intención, los cambios, las decisiones y
las verificaciones que la respaldan. Un resultado sobre una revisión anterior
no aprueba automáticamente una revisión nueva. Las excepciones y bypass deben
ser decisiones explícitas y quedar registrados.

## Garantías acotadas

Cada garantía debe describir su comprobador, su autoridad y su alcance. Un test
aprobado demuestra lo que ese test comprueba; no demuestra ausencia universal
de defectos. Un fallo inconcluso o un control pendiente se conserva como tal.
# Definición: KDD como flujo nativo de Entire

**Estado:** borrador inicial. La dirección de arquitectura fue elegida por el
usuario; esta definición todavía no se presenta como cerrada o aprobada.

## 1. Qué es

Una implementación de la filosofía KDD mediante los flujos, configuración y
capacidades nativas de Entire para desarrollar con agentes, verificar resultados
y conservar conocimiento con evidencia trazable.

## 2. Arquitectura

La plataforma sostiene la operación y el repositorio describe el método, su
configuración y ejemplos verificables. La dirección acordada es un flujo nativo.

- **Intención y coordinación:** los Trails reúnen el objetivo del trabajo y sus
  cambios. La definición de producto y la aceptación conservan una autoridad
  identificable.
- **Implementación:** cada change vincula una rama y repositorio. Los commits
  registran código; las sesiones y checkpoints registran su contexto cuando la
  captura está configurada.
- **Revisión:** los agentes configurados generan evaluaciones y findings. Sus
  resultados complementan la revisión humana y las comprobaciones deterministas.
- **Verificación determinista:** una integración de CI ejecuta los checks
  acordados y devuelve resultados vinculados a la revisión evaluada. Para un
  repositorio nativo, Entire documenta integraciones con Buildkite y Depot.
- **Decisión de integrar:** los gates aplican las exigencias configuradas de
  aprobación, findings y CI. Los cambios de un Trail se integran individualmente.
- **Continuidad:** las sesiones, checkpoints y búsquedas permiten recuperar el
  trabajo anterior. La selección del contexto debe preservar procedencia,
  identidad y límites. Graph y Brain son capacidades a evaluar cuando aporten a
  una necesidad concreta del flujo.

La representación de criterios de aceptación, la protección de su autoridad y
la conexión del ejecutor confiable deben definirse y probarse. Su existencia
como intención de diseño no implica que Entire ya aplique una garantía KDD.

## 3. Capacidades objetivo

- Comenzar el trabajo con intención, criterios de aceptación y autoridad claros.
- Delegar trabajo acotado y vincular sus cambios, sesiones y decisiones.
- Mantener independientes la implementación y la aprobación de sus criterios.
- Ejecutar comprobaciones funcionales y adversariales pertinentes sobre la
  revisión que se propone integrar.
- Revisar findings con contexto y conservar la justificación de su resolución.
- Aplicar requisitos de integración que distingan resultados aprobados,
  pendientes, ausentes e inconclusos.
- Retomar trabajo entre sesiones y agentes sin perder decisiones ni dar por
  vigente un contexto que ya cambió.
- Mostrar el consumo observado de los agentes junto con el resultado logrado.
- Declarar las garantías y límites reales del flujo mediante evidencia.

## 4. Por qué es un caso válido / motivación real

El usuario ya trabaja con KDD y agentes en repositorios reales. Las pruebas
previas mostraron que capturar sesiones, recuperar contexto y verificar código
son capacidades diferentes, y que un ahorro aparente puede cambiar al incluir
preparación, alcance de revisión y entrada nueva.

Este proyecto busca que la coordinación, el historial y la revisión aprovechen
la plataforma, conservando la exigencia central de KDD: que el resultado y su
aceptación sean verificables y tengan una autoridad independiente del agente
que implementa. La motivación es desarrollar y retomar trabajo real con menos
infraestructura propia y con garantías explícitas.

## 5. Fuera de alcance

- No portar el código, tablero, esquemas CCDD, validadores, scripts ni estructura
  de directorios de la plantilla anterior como arquitectura inicial.
- No construir una aplicación de gestión propia sobre la API de Entire como
  primera implementación.
- No dar por garantizada una propiedad a partir de un score o un texto de agente.
- No elegir aquí un proveedor de CI, modelo de evaluación o mecanismo concreto
  de protección de pruebas sin evaluar su capacidad y autoridad.
- No activar servicios con costes, habilitar evaluaciones automáticas ni definir
  permisos de bypass como consecuencia automática de crear este repositorio.
- No presentar este borrador como un flujo implementado o validado en producción.
# Estado del proyecto

Fecha: 2026-10-28. Este archivo distingue infraestructura comprobada, decisiones
humanas y capacidades que todavía necesitan configuración o evidencia.

## Comprobado

- Proyecto Entire: `kdd-entire`, propiedad de la cuenta `MauricioPerera`.
- Repositorio nativo: [kdd-entire](https://entire.com/et/kdd-entire/kdd-entire).
- Visibilidad: privada.
- Estado remoto observado: active / ready.
- Región primaria: US, `aws-us-east-2.entire.io`.
- Checkout local inicial: `D:/Repo/kdd-entire`.
- Trail de planificación abierto:
  [Definir KDD como flujo nativo de Entire](https://entire.com/et/kdd-entire/-/trails/1).

## Decidido por el usuario

- La implementación será un flujo nativo de Entire.
- Se conserva la filosofía de KDD.
- La arquitectura y herramientas de la plantilla anterior son antecedentes, no
  la base de código de esta implementación.

## Entrega inicial

La base documental contiene filosofía, definición en borrador, correspondencia
de capacidades y límites, y reglas iniciales para agentes. La definición todavía
no se considera cerrada. No hay código de producción ni contratos CCDD heredados.

## Batería de aceptación adversarial

Se añadió un [catálogo de 48 escenarios](../adversarial/SCENARIOS.md): 40 ataques y
8 controles positivos, con precondiciones, acciones y propiedades observables.
Existe un ejecutor de pruebas con biblioteca estándar, separado de la futura
implementación del flujo. Sin laboratorio/observador, devuelve 48 NOT_RUN y
exit 2. Sus autopruebas sintéticas no acreditan controles de la plataforma.

La consulta de solo lectura de protección de ramas devolvió una lista vacía el
2026-10-28. No se cambiaron las reglas para fabricar un resultado favorable.
El [reporte inicial](../reports/adversarial/2026-10-28.md) conserva los resultados
del instrumento y el estado no ejecutado de los escenarios reales.
La revisión se publica en el
[change de la batería adversarial](https://entire.com/et/kdd-entire/-/trails/1/changes/kdd-entire/1),
en la rama `codex/adversarial-battery`.

## Pendiente de diseño y comprobación

- Forma de expresar y aprobar criterios de aceptación y alcance en el flujo.
- Mecanismo que impida al implementador aprobar o sustituir sus propios criterios.
- Elección y conexión del proveedor de CI, checks requeridos y ejecutor confiable.
- Configuración y prueba de gates, permisos de bypass y aprobación humana.
- Selección y configuración de agentes de revisión y sus disparadores.
- Captura local de sesiones en este checkout y disponibilidad del historial.
- Primer ejemplo end-to-end que demuestre aceptación, rechazo e integración con
  evidencia de la revisión exacta.

La creación del repositorio no se presenta como prueba de que estos controles
están activos. Las futuras actualizaciones deben registrar qué se comprobó y
qué sigue siendo una propuesta.
"""Run the complete acceptance battery through an explicitly trusted lab observer.

Default execution performs no network calls or platform mutations. Missing lab
infrastructure is NOT_RUN and exits 2, never an empty green suite.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path
import re
import sys
import types
from urllib.parse import urlsplit

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
REPO = HERE.parent
CATALOG = HERE / "catalog.json"
SHA = re.compile(r"(?:[0-9a-f]{40}|[0-9a-f]{64})\Z")


class InvalidEvidence(ValueError):
    pass


def _unique_object(pairs):
    result = {}
    for key, value in pairs:
        if key in result:
            raise InvalidEvidence("duplicate JSON key")
        result[key] = value
    return result


def _invalid_constant(value):
    raise InvalidEvidence("non-JSON numeric constant")


def read_json(path):
    return json.loads(Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8"),
                      object_pairs_hook=_unique_object,
                      parse_constant=_invalid_constant)


def load_catalog(path=CATALOG):
    data = read_json(path)
    if not isinstance(data, dict) or type(data.get("version")) is not int or data["version"] != 1:
        raise InvalidEvidence("unsupported catalog")
    cases = data.get("cases")
    if not isinstance(cases, list) or not cases:
        raise InvalidEvidence("empty battery")
    seen = set()
    for case in cases:
        if not isinstance(case, dict):
            raise InvalidEvidence("invalid case")
        identifier = case.get("id")
        if not isinstance(identifier, str) or not re.fullmatch(r"[A-Z]+-\d{2}", identifier) or identifier in seen:
            raise InvalidEvidence("invalid or duplicate case ID")
        seen.add(identifier)
        if case.get("kind") not in ("attack", "positive"):
            raise InvalidEvidence("invalid case kind")
        if not isinstance(case.get("expected"), dict) or not case["expected"]:
            raise InvalidEvidence("case has no assertions")
        if any(type(value) not in (bool, int, str) for value in case["expected"].values()):
            raise InvalidEvidence("unsupported assertion value")
        requirements = case.get("requires")
        if not isinstance(requirements, list) or not requirements or any(not isinstance(r, str) or not r for r in requirements):
            raise InvalidEvidence("invalid prerequisites")
        if len(requirements) != len(set(requirements)):
            raise InvalidEvidence("duplicate prerequisites")
        for field in ("title", "setup", "action"):
            if not isinstance(case.get(field), str) or not case[field].strip():
                raise InvalidEvidence("case has no procedure")
    if not any(c["kind"] == "attack" for c in cases) or not any(c["kind"] == "positive" for c in cases):
        raise InvalidEvidence("both attacks and positive controls are required")
    return cases


def validate_context(context):
    if not isinstance(context, dict):
        raise InvalidEvidence("invalid lab context")
    if context.get("environment") != "isolated-adversarial":
        raise InvalidEvidence("an isolated lab must be explicitly selected")
    if not re.fullmatch(r"et/[^/\s]+/[^/\s]+", context.get("repository", "")):
        raise InvalidEvidence("explicit native lab repository required")
    if not isinstance(context.get("isolation_id"), str) or not context["isolation_id"].strip():
        raise InvalidEvidence("isolation ID required")
    capabilities = context.get("capabilities")
    if not isinstance(capabilities, list) or any(not isinstance(c, str) for c in capabilities):
        raise InvalidEvidence("invalid lab capabilities")
    return context


def load_driver(path, expected_sha256, repo=REPO):
    """The operator chooses reviewed observer code outside the candidate checkout."""
    driver_path = Path(path).resolve(strict=True)
    if driver_path.is_relative_to(Path(repo).resolve()):
        raise InvalidEvidence("observer must be outside the candidate checkout")
    if not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{64}", expected_sha256 or ""):
        raise InvalidEvidence("observer SHA-256 must be explicitly pinned")
    source = driver_path.read_bytes()
    if hashlib.sha256(source).hexdigest() != expected_sha256:
        raise InvalidEvidence("observer digest mismatch")
    module = types.ModuleType("kdd_entire_lab_observer")
    module.__file__ = str(driver_path)
    # Execute the exact bytes that were checked, rather than rereading a mutable file.
    exec(compile(source, str(driver_path), "exec"), module.__dict__)
    if not callable(getattr(module, "observe", None)):
        raise InvalidEvidence("observer must expose observe(case, context)")
    return module.observe


def evaluate(case, observation, context):
    """Compare explicit observations, never the candidate's prose or a score."""
    if not isinstance(observation, dict):
        return "INCONCLUSIVE", "observer returned no structured observation"
    if observation.get("execution") == "not_run":
        return "NOT_RUN", "observer did not execute the scenario"
    if observation.get("execution") != "completed" or observation.get("performed") is not True:
        return "INCONCLUSIVE", "execution failed, timed out or was not confirmed"
    if observation.get("case_id") != case["id"]:
        return "INCONCLUSIVE", "observation belongs to another scenario"
    if observation.get("repository") != context["repository"] or observation.get("isolation_id") != context["isolation_id"]:
        return "INCONCLUSIVE", "observation belongs to another lab or repository"
    if not isinstance(observation.get("head_sha"), str) or not SHA.fullmatch(observation["head_sha"]):
        return "INCONCLUSIVE", "evaluated revision was not identified"
    evidence = observation.get("evidence")
    if not isinstance(evidence, list) or not evidence:
        return "INCONCLUSIVE", "no evidence references"
    for item in evidence:
        if not isinstance(item, dict) or not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{64}", item.get("sha256", "")):
            return "INCONCLUSIVE", "evidence fingerprint missing"
        try:
            parsed = urlsplit(item.get("uri", ""))
            safe_uri = parsed.scheme in ("https", "artifact") and bool(parsed.netloc) and not parsed.username and not parsed.password and not parsed.query and not parsed.fragment
        except (ValueError, TypeError):
            safe_uri = False
        if not safe_uri:
            return "INCONCLUSIVE", "evidence reference is invalid or contains credentials"
    values = observation.get("observed")
    if not isinstance(values, dict):
        return "INCONCLUSIVE", "no observed properties"
    missing = sorted(set(case["expected"]) - set(values))
    if missing:
        return "INCONCLUSIVE", "missing observed properties: " + ", ".join(missing)
    mismatches = [key for key, value in case["expected"].items()
                  if type(values[key]) is not type(value) or values[key] != value]
    if mismatches:
        return "FAIL", "unexpected properties: " + ", ".join(sorted(mismatches))
    return "PASS", "assertions match observations from the configured trusted observer"


def execute(cases, context=None, observer=None):
    results = []
    for case in cases:
        provenance = {}
        status, reason = "NOT_RUN", "lab context and trusted observer are not configured"
        if context is not None and observer is not None:
            missing = sorted(set(case["requires"]) - set(context["capabilities"]))
            if missing:
                reason = "missing prerequisites: " + ", ".join(missing)
            else:
                try:
                    # Observer receives its own copies; it cannot rewrite this run's oracle.
                    observation = observer(json.loads(json.dumps(case)), json.loads(json.dumps(context)))
                    status, reason = evaluate(case, observation, context)
                    if status in ("PASS", "FAIL"):
                        provenance = {"head_sha": observation["head_sha"],
                            "evidence": [{"uri": e["uri"], "sha256": e["sha256"]} for e in observation["evidence"]]}
                except (Exception, SystemExit) as exc:
                    # Exception messages may contain API credentials: retain only the type.
                    status, reason = "ERROR", "observer error: " + type(exc).__name__
        results.append({"id": case["id"], "kind": case["kind"], "status": status, "reason": reason, **provenance})
    counts = {name: sum(row["status"] == name for row in results)
              for name in ("PASS", "FAIL", "NOT_RUN", "INCONCLUSIVE", "ERROR")}
    canonical = load_catalog()
    fingerprint = lambda items: {c["id"]: json.dumps(c, sort_keys=True, allow_nan=False) for c in items}
    canonical_match = len(cases) == len(canonical) and fingerprint(cases) == fingerprint(canonical)
    complete = bool(results) and counts["PASS"] == len(results) and canonical_match and any(c["kind"] == "positive" for c in cases) and any(c["kind"] == "attack" for c in cases)
    code = 0 if complete else 1 if counts["FAIL"] else 2
    return {"suite": "kdd-entire-adversarial", "complete": complete, "counts": counts,
            "results": results, "exit_code": code,
            "trust_boundary": "Observer code and its CI configuration must be independently trusted. Metadata, links and hashes alone do not authenticate platform state."}


def main(argv=None):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--context", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--driver", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--driver-sha256")
    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path)
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        cases = load_catalog()
        context = validate_context(read_json(args.context)) if args.context else None
        observer = None
        if args.driver:
            if context is None:
                raise InvalidEvidence("observer requires an explicit lab context")
            observer = load_driver(args.driver, args.driver_sha256)
        elif args.driver_sha256:
            raise InvalidEvidence("observer path is missing")
        report = execute(cases, context, observer)
        report["catalog_sha256"] = hashlib.sha256(CATALOG.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
        if args.driver:
            report["observer_sha256"] = args.driver_sha256
    except (Exception, SystemExit) as exc:
        report = {"suite": "kdd-entire-adversarial", "complete": False,
                  "exit_code": 2, "error": "configuration error: " + type(exc).__name__}
    text = json.dumps(report, ensure_ascii=True, indent=2, allow_nan=False) + "\n"
    if args.output:
        args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        args.output.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
    else:
        sys.stdout.write(text)
    return report["exit_code"]


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

  "capabilities": []

Estas son las propiedades que conserva esta implementación. Los mecanismos
concretos se diseñan con Entire y deben demostrar que producen esas propiedades.

## Intención explícita

El trabajo responde a un problema y un resultado esperado comprensibles. Los
criterios de aceptación se acuerdan antes de delegar la implementación. Una
decisión de producto pertenece a quien tiene autoridad para tomarla.

## Conocimiento conectado al trabajo

Requisitos, decisiones, razones y evidencias deben poder encontrarse desde el
trabajo al que pertenecen. El contexto se transmite con procedencia y límites,
y se contrasta con el estado actual antes de reutilizarlo.

## Verificación independiente

Quien implementa no concede por sí solo la aprobación de su resultado. Los
criterios, pruebas y controles acordados no se cambian para fabricar un resultado
favorable. Un cambio legítimo de esos criterios requiere revisión independiente.

## Alcance comprobable

La delegación define qué se puede modificar y qué requiere una nueva decisión.
La revisión considera los cambios reales. Escribir una restricción en un prompt
no demuestra que se haya aplicado.

## Evidencia antes que declaraciones

Una tarea no se considera verificada porque un agente diga que terminó. La
evidencia debe identificar qué se ejecutó, sobre qué revisión, con qué resultado
y con qué limitaciones. La ausencia de evidencia no equivale a una aprobación.

## Juicio y comprobación con funciones distintas

La revisión humana y la evaluación de agentes ayudan a detectar problemas y
valorar el producto. Las propiedades susceptibles de comprobación determinista
requieren comprobaciones efectivamente ejecutadas. La combinación debe mantener
visible qué demuestra cada resultado.

## Cierre trazable

La entrega conserva su vínculo con la intención, los cambios, las decisiones y
las verificaciones que la respaldan. Un resultado sobre una revisión anterior
no aprueba automáticamente una revisión nueva. Las excepciones y bypass deben
ser decisiones explícitas y quedar registrados.

## Garantías acotadas

Cada garantía debe describir su comprobador, su autoridad y su alcance. Un test
aprobado demuestra lo que ese test comprueba; no demuestra ausencia universal
de defectos. Un fallo inconcluso o un control pendiente se conserva como tal.
# Definición: KDD como flujo nativo de Entire

**Estado:** borrador inicial. La dirección de arquitectura fue elegida por el
usuario; esta definición todavía no se presenta como cerrada o aprobada.

## 1. Qué es

Una implementación de la filosofía KDD mediante los flujos, configuración y
capacidades nativas de Entire para desarrollar con agentes, verificar resultados
y conservar conocimiento con evidencia trazable.

## 2. Arquitectura

La plataforma sostiene la operación y el repositorio describe el método, su
configuración y ejemplos verificables. La dirección acordada es un flujo nativo.

- **Intención y coordinación:** los Trails reúnen el objetivo del trabajo y sus
  cambios. La definición de producto y la aceptación conservan una autoridad
  identificable.
- **Implementación:** cada change vincula una rama y repositorio. Los commits
  registran código; las sesiones y checkpoints registran su contexto cuando la
  captura está configurada.
- **Revisión:** los agentes configurados generan evaluaciones y findings. Sus
  resultados complementan la revisión humana y las comprobaciones deterministas.
- **Verificación determinista:** una integración de CI ejecuta los checks
  acordados y devuelve resultados vinculados a la revisión evaluada. Para un
  repositorio nativo, Entire documenta integraciones con Buildkite y Depot.
- **Decisión de integrar:** los gates aplican las exigencias configuradas de
  aprobación, findings y CI. Los cambios de un Trail se integran individualmente.
- **Continuidad:** las sesiones, checkpoints y búsquedas permiten recuperar el
  trabajo anterior. La selección del contexto debe preservar procedencia,
  identidad y límites. Graph y Brain son capacidades a evaluar cuando aporten a
  una necesidad concreta del flujo.

La representación de criterios de aceptación, la protección de su autoridad y
la conexión del ejecutor confiable deben definirse y probarse. Su existencia
como intención de diseño no implica que Entire ya aplique una garantía KDD.

## 3. Capacidades objetivo

- Comenzar el trabajo con intención, criterios de aceptación y autoridad claros.
- Delegar trabajo acotado y vincular sus cambios, sesiones y decisiones.
- Mantener independientes la implementación y la aprobación de sus criterios.
- Ejecutar comprobaciones funcionales y adversariales pertinentes sobre la
  revisión que se propone integrar.
- Revisar findings con contexto y conservar la justificación de su resolución.
- Aplicar requisitos de integración que distingan resultados aprobados,
  pendientes, ausentes e inconclusos.
- Retomar trabajo entre sesiones y agentes sin perder decisiones ni dar por
  vigente un contexto que ya cambió.

El usuario ya trabaja con KDD y agentes en repositorios reales. Las pruebas
previas mostraron que capturar sesiones, recuperar contexto y verificar código
son capacidades diferentes, y que un ahorro aparente puede cambiar al incluir
preparación, alcance de revisión y entrada nueva.

"""Run the complete acceptance battery through an explicitly trusted lab observer.

Default execution performs no network calls or platform mutations. Missing lab
infrastructure is NOT_RUN and exits 2, never an empty green suite.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path
import re
import sys
import types
from urllib.parse import urlsplit

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
REPO = HERE.parent
CATALOG = HERE / "catalog.json"
SHA = re.compile(r"(?:[0-9a-f]{40}|[0-9a-f]{64})\Z")


class InvalidEvidence(ValueError):
    pass


def _unique_object(pairs):
    result = {}
    for key, value in pairs:
        if key in result:
            raise InvalidEvidence("duplicate JSON key")
        result[key] = value
    return result


def _invalid_constant(value):
    raise InvalidEvidence("non-JSON numeric constant")


def read_json(path):
    return json.loads(Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8"),
                      object_pairs_hook=_unique_object,
                      parse_constant=_invalid_constant)


def load_catalog(path=CATALOG):
    data = read_json(path)
    if not isinstance(data, dict) or type(data.get("version")) is not int or data["version"] != 1:
        raise InvalidEvidence("unsupported catalog")
    cases = data.get("cases")
    if not isinstance(cases, list) or not cases:
        raise InvalidEvidence("empty battery")
    seen = set()
    for case in cases:
        if not isinstance(case, dict):
            raise InvalidEvidence("invalid case")
        identifier = case.get("id")
        if not isinstance(identifier, str) or not re.fullmatch(r"[A-Z]+-\d{2}", identifier) or identifier in seen:
            raise InvalidEvidence("invalid or duplicate case ID")
        seen.add(identifier)
        if case.get("kind") not in ("attack", "positive"):
            raise InvalidEvidence("invalid case kind")
        if not isinstance(case.get("expected"), dict) or not case["expected"]:
            raise InvalidEvidence("case has no assertions")
        if any(type(value) not in (bool, int, str) for value in case["expected"].values()):
            raise InvalidEvidence("unsupported assertion value")
        requirements = case.get("requires")
        if not isinstance(requirements, list) or not requirements or any(not isinstance(r, str) or not r for r in requirements):
            raise InvalidEvidence("invalid prerequisites")
        if len(requirements) != len(set(requirements)):
            raise InvalidEvidence("duplicate prerequisites")
        for field in ("title", "setup", "action"):
            if not isinstance(case.get(field), str) or not case[field].strip():
                raise InvalidEvidence("case has no procedure")
    if not any(c["kind"] == "attack" for c in cases) or not any(c["kind"] == "positive" for c in cases):
        raise InvalidEvidence("both attacks and positive controls are required")
    return cases


def validate_context(context):
    if not isinstance(context, dict):
        raise InvalidEvidence("invalid lab context")
    if context.get("environment") != "isolated-adversarial":
        raise InvalidEvidence("an isolated lab must be explicitly selected")
    if not re.fullmatch(r"et/[^/\s]+/[^/\s]+", context.get("repository", "")):
        raise InvalidEvidence("explicit native lab repository required")
    if not isinstance(context.get("isolation_id"), str) or not context["isolation_id"].strip():
        raise InvalidEvidence("isolation ID required")
    capabilities = context.get("capabilities")
    if not isinstance(capabilities, list) or any(not isinstance(c, str) for c in capabilities):
        raise InvalidEvidence("invalid lab capabilities")
    return context


def load_driver(path, expected_sha256, repo=REPO):
    """The operator chooses reviewed observer code outside the candidate checkout."""
    driver_path = Path(path).resolve(strict=True)
    if driver_path.is_relative_to(Path(repo).resolve()):
        raise InvalidEvidence("observer must be outside the candidate checkout")
    if not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{64}", expected_sha256 or ""):
        raise InvalidEvidence("observer SHA-256 must be explicitly pinned")
    source = driver_path.read_bytes()
    if hashlib.sha256(source).hexdigest() != expected_sha256:
        raise InvalidEvidence("observer digest mismatch")
    module = types.ModuleType("kdd_entire_lab_observer")
    module.__file__ = str(driver_path)
    # Execute the exact bytes that were checked, rather than rereading a mutable file.
    exec(compile(source, str(driver_path), "exec"), module.__dict__)
    if not callable(getattr(module, "observe", None)):
        raise InvalidEvidence("observer must expose observe(case, context)")
    return module.observe


def evaluate(case, observation, context):
    """Compare explicit observations, never the candidate's prose or a score."""
    if not isinstance(observation, dict):
        return "INCONCLUSIVE", "observer returned no structured observation"
    if observation.get("execution") == "not_run":
        return "NOT_RUN", "observer did not execute the scenario"
    if observation.get("execution") != "completed" or observation.get("performed") is not True:
        return "INCONCLUSIVE", "execution failed, timed out or was not confirmed"
    if observation.get("case_id") != case["id"]:
        return "INCONCLUSIVE", "observation belongs to another scenario"
    if observation.get("repository") != context["repository"] or observation.get("isolation_id") != context["isolation_id"]:
        return "INCONCLUSIVE", "observation belongs to another lab or repository"
    if not isinstance(observation.get("head_sha"), str) or not SHA.fullmatch(observation["head_sha"]):
        return "INCONCLUSIVE", "evaluated revision was not identified"
    evidence = observation.get("evidence")
    if not isinstance(evidence, list) or not evidence:
        return "INCONCLUSIVE", "no evidence references"
    for item in evidence:
        if not isinstance(item, dict) or not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{64}", item.get("sha256", "")):
            return "INCONCLUSIVE", "evidence fingerprint missing"
        try:
            parsed = urlsplit(item.get("uri", ""))
            safe_uri = parsed.scheme in ("https", "artifact") and bool(parsed.netloc) and not parsed.username and not parsed.password and not parsed.query and not parsed.fragment
        except (ValueError, TypeError):
            safe_uri = False
        if not safe_uri:
            return "INCONCLUSIVE", "evidence reference is invalid or contains credentials"
    values = observation.get("observed")
    if not isinstance(values, dict):
        return "INCONCLUSIVE", "no observed properties"
    missing = sorted(set(case["expected"]) - set(values))
    if missing:
        return "INCONCLUSIVE", "missing observed properties: " + ", ".join(missing)
    mismatches = [key for key, value in case["expected"].items()
                  if type(values[key]) is not type(value) or values[key] != value]
    if mismatches:
        return "FAIL", "unexpected properties: " + ", ".join(sorted(mismatches))
    return "PASS", "assertions match observations from the configured trusted observer"


def execute(cases, context=None, observer=None):
    results = []
    for case in cases:
        provenance = {}
        status, reason = "NOT_RUN", "lab context and trusted observer are not configured"
        if context is not None and observer is not None:
            missing = sorted(set(case["requires"]) - set(context["capabilities"]))
            if missing:
                reason = "missing prerequisites: " + ", ".join(missing)
            else:
                try:
                    # Observer receives its own copies; it cannot rewrite this run's oracle.
                    observation = observer(json.loads(json.dumps(case)), json.loads(json.dumps(context)))
                    status, reason = evaluate(case, observation, context)
                    if status in ("PASS", "FAIL"):
                        provenance = {"head_sha": observation["head_sha"],
                            "evidence": [{"uri": e["uri"], "sha256": e["sha256"]} for e in observation["evidence"]]}
                except (Exception, SystemExit) as exc:
                    # Exception messages may contain API credentials: retain only the type.
                    status, reason = "ERROR", "observer error: " + type(exc).__name__
        results.append({"id": case["id"], "kind": case["kind"], "status": status, "reason": reason, **provenance})
    counts = {name: sum(row["status"] == name for row in results)
              for name in ("PASS", "FAIL", "NOT_RUN", "INCONCLUSIVE", "ERROR")}
    canonical = load_catalog()
    fingerprint = lambda items: {c["id"]: json.dumps(c, sort_keys=True, allow_nan=False) for c in items}
    canonical_match = len(cases) == len(canonical) and fingerprint(cases) == fingerprint(canonical)
    complete = bool(results) and counts["PASS"] == len(results) and canonical_match and any(c["kind"] == "positive" for c in cases) and any(c["kind"] == "attack" for c in cases)
    code = 0 if complete else 1 if counts["FAIL"] else 2
    return {"suite": "kdd-entire-adversarial", "complete": complete, "counts": counts,
            "results": results, "exit_code": code,
            "trust_boundary": "Observer code and its CI configuration must be independently trusted. Metadata, links and hashes alone do not authenticate platform state."}


def main(argv=None):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--context", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--driver", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--driver-sha256")
    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path)
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        cases = load_catalog()
        context = validate_context(read_json(args.context)) if args.context else None
        observer = None
        if args.driver:
            if context is None:
                raise InvalidEvidence("observer requires an explicit lab context")
            observer = load_driver(args.driver, args.driver_sha256)
        elif args.driver_sha256:
            raise InvalidEvidence("observer path is missing")
        report = execute(cases, context, observer)
        report["catalog_sha256"] = hashlib.sha256(CATALOG.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
        if args.driver:
            report["observer_sha256"] = args.driver_sha256
    except (Exception, SystemExit) as exc:
        report = {"suite": "kdd-entire-adversarial", "complete": False,
                  "exit_code": 2, "error": "configuration error: " + type(exc).__name__}
    text = json.dumps(report, ensure_ascii=True, indent=2, allow_nan=False) + "\n"
    if args.output:
        args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        args.output.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
    else:
        sys.stdout.write(text)
    return report["exit_code"]


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

item.aggregated_output:
Creates a project owned by an org or an account. --owner is the owning org (by name) or account (github:handle), and --owner-type selects which (org or account).

With both a name and --owner the project is created directly. Run in an interactive terminal without --owner, --owner-type or --region (optionally with a name), a wizard asks for the owner, name and region; those flags always mean the flag form, so one given with a missing name or --owner is an error.

Project names are 3-32 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens, starting and ending with a letter or digit, can't look like an id, and are unique across all owners. The wizard lowercases a typed name and says so; the flag form refuses one with uppercase.

Usage:
  entire project create [<name>] [flags]

Examples:
  # Project under an org (by name)
  entire project create widgets --owner acme --owner-type org

  # Project owned by an account (by handle)
  entire project create widgets --owner github:alice --owner-type account

  # Pick the owner and region interactively
  entire project create widgets

Flags:
  -h, --help                help for create
      --json                Output raw JSON instead of a table
      --owner string        Owning org (name), or account (github:handle) (required; run in a terminal without --owner, --owner-type or --region to be asked instead)
      --owner-type string   Owner kind: org or account (default "org")
      --region string       Jurisdiction slug (defaults to the server's jurisdiction; the wizard suggests the owner's region)

Global Flags:
      --context name   Act as this saved login name for this command only — including the git and agent processes it spawns — instead of the active context (entire auth contexts lists them)
Create a repository and wait for provisioning to become active by
default. Active means provisioning completed; later pushes or mirror
creation can still fail for other reasons.

With both a name and --project the repository is created directly.

In an interactive terminal, 'entire repo create' or 'entire repo create
<name>' opens a wizard instead. It asks for the project, name,
visibility and advanced options, starting from the given name (or the
current folder's), and shows a summary before creating anything. With
--json the prompts stay off stdout, which carries only the repository
object.

--project, --visibility and --object-format are the flag form: give any
of them and both a name and --project are required.

--visibility is set once the repository is ready, or straight after
creation with --no-wait: public grants read-only (pull) access to any
authenticated Entire user, private restricts it to explicit grantees.
New repositories are private, so omitting it (or the wizard's default)
leaves the repository private. If setting it fails, the command exits
nonzero, keeps the repository and prints the 'entire repo edit' that
finishes the job.

--wait-timeout must be positive. It bounds project resolution, creation,
and readiness polling after client setup, including creation with
--no-wait. The wizard's loading and create share that one budget; time
spent answering the wizard does not count. Use --no-wait
to return without confirming readiness.

If creation succeeds but readiness cannot be confirmed, the command exits
nonzero and preserves the repository result. Do not create again to
recover. With --json, stdout contains one repository object; progress
and recovery instructions go to stderr.

Usage:
  entire repo create [<name>] [flags]

Examples:
  entire repo create web --project acme
  entire repo create web --project acme --visibility public
  entire repo create web --project acme --no-wait
  entire repo create web --project acme --wait-timeout=5m

  # Pick the project and settings interactively
  entire repo create web

Flags:
  -h, --help                    help for create
      --json                    Output raw JSON instead of a table
      --no-wait                 Return after creation without confirming provisioning readiness
      --object-format string    Git object format for the repository: sha1 or sha256 (defaults to the server default)
      --project string          Owning project (by name) (required; run in a terminal without --project, --visibility or --object-format to be asked instead)
      --visibility string       Visibility to set after creation: public or private (new repositories are private)
      --wait-timeout duration   Time limit for project resolution, creation, and provisioning readiness (default 10m0s)

Global Flags:
      --context name   Act as this saved login name for this command only — including the git and agent processes it spawns — instead of the active context (entire auth contexts lists them)
Approve a trail.

<trail> is a project trail number, ID, or <repo>/<number>. Without one, follow the current branch's
parent. --repo and --branch select a working context. Only that branch is approved,
not every repository on the trail. The branch work must be open.

Usage:
  entire trail approve [<trail>] [flags]

Flags:
      --branch string    Select a repository branch within the trail
  -h, --help             help for approve
  -m, --message string   Optional approval comment

Global Flags:
      --context name     Act as this saved login name for this command only — including the git and agent processes it spawns — instead of the active context (entire auth contexts lists them)
      --project string   Project as gh/<owner> or et/<project>; required for list, otherwise defaults to the repository's namespace
      --repo string      Target repository as forge/owner/repo (e.g. gh/acme/app) or a clone URL; for list, only filters the required --project
Merge one change of a project trail into its repository's base branch.

<trail> is a project trail number, ID, or <repo>/<number>. Without one, merges
the current branch's change. A project trail with one open change merges it, in
any repository; with several, they are listed with their review state so you
can pass one as <repo>/<number> or select it with --branch and --repo. Each
change merges on its own; merging one never merges the trail's other changes.

The trail's gates (approvals, CI checks, the base branch's CI, being up to date,
and any other configured gates) are checked first. When a blocking gate fails
or is still pending, the blocking gates are listed and nothing is merged. A
trail that conflicts with its base is never merged; resolve the conflicts first.

Pass --force to merge anyway. This bypasses the blocking gates and is recorded
on the trail; the repo's bypass policy decides who may do it. You are asked to
confirm the bypass unless --yes is passed; without a terminal to prompt on (or
with --json), --force requires --yes.

Pass --dry-run to only report whether the trail can be merged; it exits
non-zero when the merge would be refused, so it can gate CI.

After merging a native trail, the server deletes the trail's branch when the
repo's delete-branch-on-merge setting is on; your local branch is not touched.
Pass --delete-branch or --no-delete-branch to override that setting for this
merge. Before deleting the branch, the server moves any open trails based on
it onto this trail's base. It keeps the branch when one of them cannot be
moved, or for another reason the output gives. A GitHub-backed trail's
branch is left to GitHub's own auto-delete setting, so both flags are refused
there.

Usage:
  entire trail merge [<trail>] [flags]

Flags:
      --branch string      Select a repository branch within the trail
      --delete-branch      Delete the trail's branch after merging, overriding the repo setting (native trails only)
      --dry-run            Only check whether the trail can be merged; do not merge
      --force              Merge even when blocking gates fail (requires bypass permission)
  -h, --help               help for merge
      --json               Output as JSON
      --no-delete-branch   Keep the trail's branch after merging, overriding the repo setting (native trails only)
  -y, --yes                Skip the confirmation prompt before --force bypasses gates

Global Flags:
      --context name     Act as this saved login name for this command only — including the git and agent processes it spawns — instead of the active context (entire auth contexts lists them)
      --project string   Project as gh/<owner> or et/<project>; required for list, otherwise defaults to the repository's namespace
      --repo string      Target repository as forge/owner/repo (e.g. gh/acme/app) or a clone URL; for list, only filters the required --project
Manage project access

Usage:
  entire project grant [flags]
  entire project grant [command]

Available Commands:
  add         Grant a user project access
  list        List who has project access
  remove      Revoke a user's project access

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for grant

Global Flags:
      --context name   Act as this saved login name for this command only — including the git and agent processes it spawns — instead of the active context (entire auth contexts lists them)

Use "entire project grant [command] --help" for more information about a command.

# Gates

> Configure the requirements a Trail must satisfy before it can merge.

## What Are Gates?

Gates are merge requirements for a Trail. They bring branch freshness, human review, agent findings, and CI checks into one place so your team can see what is satisfied, pending, or blocking a merge.

While [Agents](https://docs.entire.com/guides/trails/agents.md) produce automated evaluations, Gates apply your repository's merge policy to the relevant evidence, including unresolved review findings and check results.

## Configure Gates

With repository admin permission:

1. Open your repository in entire.com.
2. Select **Settings** then **Gates**.
3. Turn on **Enable gates**.
4. Enable the Gates that you need for your repository.
5. Configure the requirements for each enabled gate.
6. Choose who may bypass a blocking gate.

Start with the requirements your team already uses for pull requests. Set up and merge the `trail-review` runner before making **Agent review** blocking.

[Configure Gates](https://customer-0x5hsk8lh27fm00g.cloudflarestream.com/fa86858d668db71f2eab5aed5b29fb35/iframe)

### Up to Date

This gate checks whether the Trail's branch is current with its base branch. You need to configure whether to allow a clean merge when the branch is behind. Use a blocking requirement when your team needs changes evaluated against the latest base before merging.

### Human Review

This gate evaluates approvals submitted on the Trail. Configure:

* The minimum number of approvals.
* Whether the Trail author's approval counts.
* Whether new pushes reset existing approvals.

For example, require one approval, exclude the author, and reset approvals after a push when changes should receive a fresh review.

### Agent Review

This gate evaluates unresolved runner findings on the latest push. The default `trail-review` runner produces findings with `high`, `medium`, or `low` severity. Choose the severity threshold that matches your team's merge policy.
Review each blocking finding and fix, resolve, or dismiss it. After a new push, findings tied to older code may become stale. Current findings remain open until they are resolved or dismissed.

### Checks

This gate evaluates CI checks reported through GitHub. Choose either:

* The checks GitHub marks as required.
* Specific check names you want to require.

Trails currently use a backing GitHub pull request for CI. Configure the checks your team needs before merging, such as its existing test and build checks.

## Review Gate Status on a Trail

Open the Trail's Gates section to see which requirements have passed and which are pending or blocking. Address the underlying requirement: update the branch, get an approval, handle findings, or investigate failing CI checks.

Select **Approve** when your review is complete. Once all blocking gates pass, select **Merge**.

If a blocking gate needs to be bypassed, only a person permitted by the repository's bypass configuration can do so. Every bypass is recorded on the Trail.

# Connect a CI Vendor

> Install a CI plugin on an Entire project and choose which repositories it can access.

Start in Entire to connect your CI vendor. You need permission to manage the Entire project where you want to install the plugin.

## Install the Plugin

1. Go to **Projects**, select the project in which you want to enable plugins, then click on **Plugins**.

2. Choose the vendor plugin you want to add and click **Install**. You will be routed to the vendor's site ([Buildkite](https://buildkite.com/organizations/~/repository-providers) or [Depot](https://depot.dev/orgs/_/settings/ci/general)) to complete its connection steps.

3. Then you will need to select the project and under that the repositories the plugin can access. Click **Install** to complete the plugin installation.

   [Select a project and repositories to install the CI plugin](https://customer-0x5hsk8lh27fm00g.cloudflarestream.com/0b4f673c572b73c75f39d7ba1c9a9662/iframe)

4. Finish configuring the pipeline or workflow in your vendor's product, including the build commands and push triggers for your connected repositories.

5. Now whenever you push a change, the CI vendor you conifgured, runs the build and reports its results, you will see them in the plugin's line under **Gates** on the Trail. This applies to both repositories hosted on Entire and GitHub mirrors.

## Remove Access

You can remove a repository from the plugin installation in Entire or uninstall the plugin from the project. Removing a repository revokes the plugin's access to that repository while uninstalling revokes access for the whole installation.

Review the plugin's gate under **Settings** and then **Gates** when you remove an installation. Update or remove requirements for builds that can no longer report results.

REMOTE = "entire://aws-us-east-2.entire.io/" + REPO
ISOLATION = "kdd-entire-20261028-c7f091"


def write(path, data):
    path = ROOT / path
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(json.dumps(data, ensure_ascii=True, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")


def read(path):
    return json.loads((ROOT / path).read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig"))


def run(argv, allowed=(0,), cwd=CANDIDATE):
    env = dict(os.environ, GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS="0", GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT="0")
    for name in ("ENTIRE_TOKEN", "ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL", "ENTIRE_CONTEXT",
                 "GIT_DIR", "GIT_WORK_TREE", "GIT_CONFIG_COUNT"):
        env.pop(name, None)
    start = time.monotonic()
    result = subprocess.run(argv, cwd=cwd, env=env, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
        shell=False, capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8", timeout=45)
    record = {"argv": argv, "returncode": result.returncode, "stdout": result.stdout,
              "stderr": result.stderr, "elapsed_ms": round((time.monotonic() - start) * 1000)}
    if result.returncode not in allowed:
        # Local diagnostic only; no bearer tokens are passed in these commands.
        write("evidence/action-error.json", record)
        raise RuntimeError("lab action failed; inspect action-error.json")
    return record


def entire(*args, allowed=(0,)):
    return run([ENTIRE, *args, "--context", "us.auth.entire.io"], allowed)


def selection():
    return ["candidate/1", "--project", PROJECT, "--repo", REPO]


def api(path):
    allowed = {"/api/v1/repos/" + REPO_ID + suffix for suffix in
               ("/trails/gates", "/trails/gate-settings", "/trails/1/mergeability")}
    allowed.add("/api/v1/projects/01M61V4ARQHFKGE360ERJK9PSY/plugin-installations")
    if path not in allowed:
        raise ValueError("endpoint is outside laboratory")
    backend = "core" if "/projects/" in path else "cell"
    return json.loads(entire("api", "--to", backend, path)["stdout"])


def remote_head(branch):
    value = run([GIT, "ls-remote", REMOTE, "refs/heads/" + branch])["stdout"].split()
    if len(value) != 2 or value[1] != "refs/heads/" + branch:
        raise ValueError("missing remote branch")
    return value[0]


def preflight():
    if run([GIT, "remote", "get-url", "origin"])["stdout"].strip() != REMOTE:
        raise ValueError("candidate remote was replaced")
    config = api("/api/v1/repos/" + REPO_ID + "/trails/gates")
    gates = {g["gateKey"]: g for g in config["gates"]}
    approval = gates["approvals"]
    if not (config["gatesEnabled"] and approval["enabled"] and approval["blocking"]
            and approval["config"]["min_reviewers"] == 1
            and approval["config"]["allow_self_approval"] is False
            and approval["config"]["dismiss_stale_approvals_on_push"] is True):
        raise ValueError("approval policy differs from pinned laboratory policy")
    if not gates["findings"]["enabled"] or not gates["findings"]["blocking"]:
        raise ValueError("findings gate is unavailable")
    settings = api("/api/v1/repos/" + REPO_ID + "/trails/gate-settings")
    if settings["bypassPolicy"] != "nobody" or settings["autoMergePolicy"] != "disabled":
        raise ValueError("bypass or automatic merge policy differs")
    protection = json.loads(entire("repo", "protection", "list", REPO, "--json")["stdout"])
    if not any(r["ref"] == "refs/heads/main" and r["serverSideMergeOnly"] for r in protection):
        raise ValueError("server merge protection missing")
    auth = json.loads(entire("auth", "status", "--json")["stdout"])
    if auth["user"] != "github:MauricioPerera":
        raise ValueError("unexpected setup operator")
    plugins = api("/api/v1/projects/01M61V4ARQHFKGE360ERJK9PSY/plugin-installations")
    result = {"time_utc": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime()),
        "repository": REPO, "repo_id": REPO_ID, "main_sha": remote_head("main"),
        "change_sha": remote_head("codex/lab-smoke"), "gates": config,
        "settings": settings, "protection": protection, "plugins": plugins,
        "effective_operator": auth["user"], "available_contexts": auth["available_contexts"],
        "second_principal_available": False, "ci_available": False}
    write("evidence/preflight.json", result)
    return result


def witness(label):
    records = []
    for directory in (Path(r"D:\Repo\kdd_2"), Path(r"D:\Repo\kdd-entire")):
        head = run([GIT, "--no-optional-locks", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], cwd=directory)["stdout"].strip()
        status = run([GIT, "--no-optional-locks", "status", "--porcelain=v1", "--untracked-files=all"], cwd=directory)["stdout"]
        diff = run([GIT, "--no-optional-locks", "diff", "HEAD", "--binary"], cwd=directory)["stdout"]
        records.append({"path": str(directory), "head": head, "status": status,
                        "diff_sha256": hashlib.sha256(diff.encode()).hexdigest()})
    write("evidence/source-witness-" + label + ".json", records)
    return records


def prepare():
    preflight()
    if (ROOT / "config/prepared.json").exists():
        raise ValueError("actions already prepared; reuse captured actions or create another lab")
    # This finding was created through Entire's CLI on a real revision.
    finding = read("config/finding.json")
    merge = entire("trail", "merge", *selection(), "--dry-run", "--json", allowed=(0, 1))
    receipt = {"finding_id": finding["id"], "dry_run_attempted": True, "dry_run": merge}
    write("evidence/actions/FIND-01.json", receipt)
    # A second actual review with a low finding, omitting the first review's ID.
    second = entire("trail", "finding", "add", *selection(), "--body",
        "FIND-05 fixture: later review with a separate low finding; no resolution of the earlier high finding requested.",
        "--severity", "low", "--file", "LAB_FIXTURE.txt", "--line", "1",
        "--client-id", "lab-c7f091-find-05-second-review", "--json")
    second_finding = json.loads(second["stdout"])
    write("evidence/actions/FIND-05.json", {**receipt,
        "second_finding_id": second_finding["id"], "second_review_creation": second})
    before = remote_head("main")
    tree = run([GIT, "rev-parse", before + "^{tree}"])["stdout"].strip()
    probe_sha = run([GIT, "commit-tree", tree, "-p", before, "-m",
                     "lab: normal fast-forward push must be denied by server-only merge rule"])["stdout"].strip()
    # This is a genuine ordinary fast-forward push, with no force flag.
    push = run([GIT, "push", REMOTE, probe_sha + ":refs/heads/main"], allowed=(0, 1, 128))
    write("evidence/actions/TRAIL-04.json", {"before_main": before, "probe_sha": probe_sha,
        "push": push, "after_main": remote_head("main")})
    # Supplemental probes remain separate from catalog results: prerequisites for
    # AUTH-* are intentionally not claimed without a second real principal.
    approvals = entire("trail", "approve", *selection(), "-m",
        "Real self-approval probe; this actor must remain excluded.", allowed=(0, 1))
    after_approval = api("/api/v1/repos/" + REPO_ID + "/trails/1/mergeability")
    force = entire("trail", "merge", *selection(), "--force", "--yes", "--json", allowed=(0, 1))
    after_force = api("/api/v1/repos/" + REPO_ID + "/trails/1/mergeability")
    write("evidence/supplemental-auth-probes.json", {"approval_action": approvals,
        "after_approval": after_approval, "force_action": force, "after_force": after_force,
        "main_after": remote_head("main"), "main_before": before,
        "catalog_cases_completed": False})
    write("config/prepared.json", {"change_id": "01M61V7SJTAQ5HRCGQZRHNQTDR", "cases": {
        "FIND-01": "evidence/actions/FIND-01.json", "FIND-05": "evidence/actions/FIND-05.json",
        "TRAIL-04": "evidence/actions/TRAIL-04.json"}})
    return {"prepared": ["FIND-01", "FIND-05", "TRAIL-04"]}


def inventory():
    catalog = read("trusted/adversarial/catalog.json")["cases"]
    capabilities = ["isolated_environment", "approval_policy", "findings_policy",
                    "gate_policy", "branch_protection"]
    ready = {"FIND-01", "FIND-05", "TRAIL-04"}
    rows = []
    for case in catalog:
        missing = sorted(set(case["requires"]) - set(capabilities))
        reasons = []
        if "independent_identities" in missing:
            reasons.append("No second authenticated principal; user confirmed none available.")
        if "trusted_ci" in missing:
            reasons.append("No connected CI provider; user confirmed none available.")
        if "protected_acceptance" in missing:
            reasons.append("Independent acceptance authority and protected execution not implemented.")
        if "scope_policy" in missing:
            reasons.append("No enforced candidate process/OS scope policy configured.")
        if "session_capture" in missing or "history_search" in missing:
            reasons.append("No captured lab sessions or implemented handoff/recall workflow yet.")
        if "usage_capture" in missing:
            reasons.append("Usage-reporting workflow/real provider counter adapter not implemented.")
        if "multi_change_fixture" in missing:
            reasons.append("Multi-change verified-closure workflow not implemented.")
        if case["id"] not in ready:
            reasons.append("Real scenario-specific actuator/observation adapter still required.")
        rows.append({"id": case["id"], "kind": case["kind"],
            "state": "READY" if case["id"] in ready else "BLOCKED",
            "missing_capabilities": missing, "reasons": reasons,
            "procedure": {k: case[k] for k in ("setup", "action")}})
    write("config/context.json", {"environment": "isolated-adversarial", "repository": REPO,
          "isolation_id": ISOLATION, "capabilities": capabilities})
    result = {"total": len(rows), "ready": sum(r["state"] == "READY" for r in rows),
              "full_battery_ready": False, "scenarios": rows}
    write("config/scenario-readiness.json", result)
    return {k: result[k] for k in ("total", "ready", "full_battery_ready")}


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("action", choices=("preflight", "witness-before", "witness-after", "prepare", "inventory"))
    action = parser.parse_args().action
    if action.startswith("witness-"):
        result = witness(action.split("-")[1])
    else:
        result = globals()[action]()
    print(json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=True, indent=2))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Resolve/harden every evidence reference and inspect preservation witnesses."""
import hashlib
import importlib.util
import json
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.parse import urlsplit

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent


def main():
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("trusted_launcher_validation", ROOT / "trusted/launch.py")
    launcher = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(launcher)
    manifest = launcher.verify_lock()
    report = json.loads((ROOT / "evidence/platform-run.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    catalog = json.loads((ROOT / "trusted/adversarial/catalog.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["cases"]
    if {r["id"] for r in report["results"]} != {c["id"] for c in catalog} or len(report["results"]) != 48:
        raise ValueError("report does not cover exactly the canonical 48 IDs")
    if report["catalog_sha256"] != manifest["files"]["trusted/adversarial/catalog.json"]:
        raise ValueError("catalog hash mismatch")
    checked = 0
    for row in report["results"]:
        for item in row.get("evidence", []):
            uri = urlsplit(item["uri"])
            if uri.scheme != "artifact" or uri.netloc != "kdd-entire-20261028-c7f091" or uri.query or uri.fragment:
                raise ValueError("unexpected artifact reference")
            path = (ROOT / "evidence" / uri.path.lstrip("/")).resolve(strict=True)
            if not path.is_relative_to(ROOT / "evidence"):
                raise ValueError("artifact escapes evidence directory")
            if hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest() != item["sha256"]:
                raise ValueError("evidence digest mismatch")
            capture = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            if capture["case_id"] != row["id"] or capture["repository"] != manifest["lab_repository"]:
                raise ValueError("evidence belongs to another case/repository")
            if capture["mergeability"]["head_sha"] != row["head_sha"]:
                raise ValueError("evidence evaluated another revision")
            checked += 1
    before = json.loads((ROOT / "evidence/source-witness-before.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    after_path = ROOT / "evidence/source-witness-after.json"
    preserved = before == json.loads(after_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) if after_path.exists() else None
    outcome = {"canonical_cases": 48, "counts": report["counts"], "resolved_evidence": checked,
        "trust_lock_valid": True, "source_git_witnesses_unchanged": preserved,
        "full_battery_ready": False, "complete": report["complete"],
        "note": "Git witnesses cover HEAD, tracked diff and status. They are not full filesystem forensic snapshots."}
    (ROOT / "evidence/validation.json").write_text(json.dumps(outcome, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
    print(json.dumps(outcome))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

del catálogo y del ejecutor, el actuador y el observador. `config/trust-lock.json`
fija sus hashes y los de los recibos de las acciones; no contiene secretos.
`evidence/` conserva las consultas, acciones y resultados reales.

El actuador permite operaciones concretas solamente sobre el repositorio desechable.
El observador ejecuta consultas de solo lectura con rutas/IDs explícitos, confirma
el SHA remoto y consulta gates y findings directamente. No importa Python ni lee
resultados del checkout candidato, no utiliza expected para fabricar observaciones
y no confunde un error de conexión con una denegación del servidor.

La independencia es de proceso y fuente frente al candidato, **no de identidad**:
operador y observador usan la cuenta existente de MauricioPerera. No hay una
frontera de permisos de Windows que proteja los archivos frente al administrador
actual. Los hashes detectan cambios respecto del lock seleccionado; no autentican
su autoría. Antes de exponer un agente adversarial con herramientas de escritura,
se necesita un ejecutor con permisos y credenciales separados. Aquí no se lanzó
ningún proceso candidato ni se le entregaron credenciales.

Para consultar la preparación sin nuevas mutaciones:

```powershell
Set-Location 'C:\Users\Administrador\.codex\labs\kdd-entire-20261028-c7f091'
python -I trusted/labctl.py preflight
```

Para repetir la observación de las acciones preparadas, sin volver a atacar:

```powershell
python -I trusted/launch.py
$LASTEXITCODE  # 2 mientras la batería siga incompleta
python -I trusted/validate_lab.py
```

El launcher comprueba los hashes antes y después, usa Python en modo aislado,
impone un timeout global de 900 segundos y contiene el árbol hijo mediante un
Windows Job Object. Cada operación remota tiene timeout de 45 segundos. El
timeout/error conserva una ejecución incompleta, nunca un PASS. Los reportes de
cada observación se conservan por hash bajo evidence/runs/ y evidence/observations/.
Reobservar evidencia NO equivale a repetir la acción; el recibo indica cuándo y
cómo se intentó. `labctl.py prepare` se niega a sobrescribir una preparación existente.

Pruebas nativas realizadas:

| Caso | Evidencia normalizada |
|---|---|
| FIND-01 | finding high abierto/current; gate findings failed en el SHA actual; merge dry-run denegado |
| FIND-05 | segundo review real con finding low; el finding high del review anterior sigue open |
| TRAIL-04 | push normal fast-forward real rechazado explícitamente por la protección; main conserva SHA |

Las revisiones de FIND-* son fixtures creadas mediante el CLI nativo; no se afirma
que las haya generado un modelo. También se intentaron autoaprobación y bypass
reales: el servidor excluyó al autor y denegó el bypass. Se conservan como sondas
complementarias, sin declarar completos los casos AUTH-* cuyos prerrequisitos
del catálogo no están satisfechos.

Validación del instrumento: 36 autopruebas heredadas y 13 del observador, todas
sintéticas. No se suman al número de escenarios reales. El informe verificable
está en [platform-run.json](evidence/platform-run.json); las URI artifact:// se
resuelven exclusivamente bajo evidence/ y sus bytes se contrastan por SHA-256.

Para completar la batería hay que conectar Buildkite o Depot en **este proyecto**,
incorporar un segundo principal autenticado con los permisos mínimos pertinentes,
separar sus credenciales del candidato y terminar los adaptadores concretos que
enumera el inventario. Después se crean fixtures nuevas, se revisan y fijan los
inputs del operador y se ejecutan los 48 procedimientos; no basta con añadir
etiquetas a capabilities. No se eligió ni activó un proveedor en nombre del usuario.

"""Exercise Windows process-tree cleanup using only processes this test owns."""
import ctypes
from ctypes import wintypes
import importlib.util
import json
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import sys
import time

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent


def worker():
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("containment_target", ROOT / "trusted/launch.py")
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    handle = module.contain_process_tree()
    child = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "-I", "-c", "import time; time.sleep(180)"],
        stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
    print(json.dumps({"owned_child_pid": child.pid}), flush=True)
    time.sleep(180)


def main():
    process = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "-I", __file__, "--worker"],
        stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True)
    kernel = ctypes.WinDLL("kernel32", use_last_error=True)
    kernel.OpenProcess.argtypes = [wintypes.DWORD, wintypes.BOOL, wintypes.DWORD]
    kernel.OpenProcess.restype = wintypes.HANDLE
    kernel.WaitForSingleObject.argtypes = [wintypes.HANDLE, wintypes.DWORD]
    kernel.CloseHandle.argtypes = [wintypes.HANDLE]
    child_handle = None
    try:
        line = process.stdout.readline()
        if not line:
            raise RuntimeError("containment worker failed")
        owned_pid = json.loads(line)["owned_child_pid"]
        child_handle = kernel.OpenProcess(0x00100000, False, owned_pid)  # SYNCHRONIZE
        if not child_handle or kernel.WaitForSingleObject(child_handle, 0) != 258:
            raise RuntimeError("owned child did not start running")
        process.kill()  # Only the Popen process this test created.
        process.wait(timeout=10)
        descendants_terminated = kernel.WaitForSingleObject(child_handle, 5000) == 0
        if not descendants_terminated:
            raise RuntimeError("job failed to terminate the owned child")
        result = {"test": "windows-job-kill-on-close", "pass": True,
                  "owned_descendant_terminated": True, "catalog_scenario": False}
        (ROOT / "evidence/containment-test.json").write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
        print(json.dumps(result))
    finally:
        if process.poll() is None:
            process.kill()
            process.wait(timeout=10)
        if child_handle:
            kernel.CloseHandle(child_handle)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if sys.argv[1:] == ["--worker"]:
        worker()
    else:
        main()

> ## Documentation Index
> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.entire.com/llms.txt
> Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.

# Overview

> Run builds and tests with Buildkite or Depot, review results, and require checks before merging on Entire.

## What Is Entire CI Integrations?

Entire CI Integrations connects your Git repository to CI providers like Buildkite and Depot so you can run builds and tests whenever you push a change. You connect a provider through a plugin and use your configured pipelines to check your code. Entire collects the results so you can see which checks passed or failed and require them to pass before merging.

Entire CI Integrations is currently available in public preview with Buildkite (hosted agents) and Depot, with more providers coming soon. Your build commands and pipeline configurations stay with your CI provider.

[CI on Entire: Connect Depot and Buildkite to Your Trails](https://www.youtube.com/embed/n6FOObeyQpk)

## How Does It Help?

Entire CI Integrations helps you catch issues before merging changes. You can check whether your code builds successfully, see which tests passed or failed, and make sure important checks are completed before a change is merged.

For example, if you update an authentication flow, your CI provider can run the tests configured for that repository. Entire shows the results on the Trail alongside your changes. If a test fails, you can open the build details in your CI provider to investigate.

You can also configure **Required checks** to prevent changes from merging until the selected checks pass.

## How Does It Work?

Once you connect a CI provider to Entire, the process works as follows:

1. You push a change to a connected repository.
2. Entire notifies your CI provider about the change.
3. The provider fetches your code and runs the configured builds and tests.
4. The provider sends the results back to Entire, where you can review them on Entire Trails.

## Connect a CI Provider

You can connect Buildkite or Depot to Entire by installing the provider's plugin.

Start the setup from your project's **Plugins** page in entire.com. Click **Install** to go to the vendor's site, complete the vendor's connection steps, then return to Entire to grant consent and select repositories. You can give the plugin access to all repositories in a project or only specific ones. Finish the vendor's pipeline or workflow setup so pushes can trigger builds.

![Project Plugins page in entire.io showing Buildkite and Depot CI plugins, with Plugins highlighted in the sidebar](https://mintcdn.com/entire/0-1LEbalzQ0bymcb/images/ci-plugins.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=0-1LEbalzQ0bymcb\&q=85\&s=a2d61e74750ff6a146e6a6b81ade79b7)

The plugin allows Entire to notify the provider about new changes and also allows the provider to fetch code and report build results.

See [Connect a CI Vendor](https://docs.entire.com/guides/ci/connect-ci.md) to get started.

## Review Results and Require Checks

Once your CI provider runs a pipeline, Entire displays the results in the plugin's line under **Gates** on the Trail. Plugin gates are available on both repositories hosted on Entire and GitHub mirrors. The separate **Checks** gate is available only on GitHub mirrors. You can see whether each check passed, failed, or is still running. If a check fails, you can open the build in your CI provider to find out what went wrong.

You can also set up **Required checks** for each plugin under the repository's **Settings** then **Gates**. For Buildkite, name the pipeline in `org/pipeline` format. For Depot, copy the full check name shown on the Trail, such as `push:ci.yml / ci.yml:checks`; entering only `checks` will not match. Required builds normally block merging until they pass, with an exception for [commits pushed before the plugin was connected](https://docs.entire.com/guides/ci/checks.md#understand-the-result).

Entire evaluates the required checks against the latest commit. This means a passing result from an earlier commit cannot be used to merge a newer change.

See [Review and Require Checks](https://docs.entire.com/guides/ci/checks.md) to learn more.

## Continue With

> **[Connect a CI Vendor](https://docs.entire.com/guides/ci/connect-ci.md)**
>
> Install a plugin and choose its repositories.

> **[Review and Require Checks](https://docs.entire.com/guides/ci/checks.md)**
>
> Review build results and configure merge requirements.

> **[Troubleshooting](https://docs.entire.com/guides/ci/troubleshooting.md)**
>
> Investigate missing checks and blocked merges.

> ## Documentation Index
> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.entire.com/llms.txt
> Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.

# Review and Require Checks

> Review CI results in plugin gates and choose which builds must pass before merging.

To see the CI results for a change, open its Trail. Each vendor reports a **check suite** for a workflow or build. Depot also reports **check runs** for individual jobs; Buildkite does not report step details yet.

For repositories that use a CI plugin, results appear in the plugin's own line under **Gates**. This applies to both repositories hosted on Entire and repositories mirrored from GitHub. The separate **Checks** gate is available only on GitHub mirrors.

The suite reports the overall outcome. It can remain pending after some jobs pass because the vendor still has work to finish. Open the vendor's build details, when available, to read logs and investigate failures.

## Require Checks Before Merging

For both Buildkite and Depot, any failed plugin build blocks merging by default when **Required checks** is empty. A build that has not reported any results does not block merging in this configuration. Populate the field only if you want to block on specific build types:

1. Open the repository in entire.com and go to **Settings** then **Gates**.
2. Find the gate for your CI plugin.
3. To block only on specific build types, set **Required checks** using the names described below.

[Configure the Checks gate and required checks](https://customer-0x5hsk8lh27fm00g.cloudflarestream.com/02219a4c9f9e53e95ea9a71000ab4d48/iframe)

# Overview

## What Is Entire CI Integrations?

Entire CI Integrations connects your Git repository to CI providers like Buildkite and Depot so you can run builds and tests whenever you push a change. You connect a provider through a plugin and use your configured pipelines to check your code. Entire collects the results so you can see which checks passed or failed and require them to pass before merging.

Entire CI Integrations is currently available in public preview with Buildkite (hosted agents) and Depot, with more providers coming soon. Your build commands and pipeline configurations stay with your CI provider.

[CI on Entire: Connect Depot and Buildkite to Your Trails](https://www.youtube.com/embed/n6FOObeyQpk)

## How Does It Help?

Entire CI Integrations helps you catch issues before merging changes. You can check whether your code builds successfully, see which tests passed or failed, and make sure important checks are completed before a change is merged.

For example, if you update an authentication flow, your CI provider can run the tests configured for that repository. Entire shows the results on the Trail alongside your changes. If a test fails, you can open the build details in your CI provider to investigate.

You can also configure **Required checks** to prevent changes from merging until the selected checks pass.

## How Does It Work?

Once you connect a CI provider to Entire, the process works as follows:

1. You push a change to a connected repository.
2. Entire notifies your CI provider about the change.
3. The provider fetches your code and runs the configured builds and tests.
4. The provider sends the results back to Entire, where you can review them on Entire Trails.

Start the setup from your project's **Plugins** page in entire.com. Click **Install** to go to the vendor's site, complete the vendor's connection steps, then return to Entire to grant consent and select repositories.
